html:
This bar follows the Russian state from Muscovy, the grand duchy around Moscow, through the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union to today's Russia. It starts in 1480, when Grand Prince Ivan III stopped paying tribute to the Mongol Golden Horde.

Moscow was a minor town in the lands of Kievan Rus' when the Mongols came. Its princes rose as tax collectors for the Horde, then gathered the other Russian principalities, taking Novgorod in 1478. Ivan III married a niece of the last Byzantine emperor, and Moscow began to see itself as heir to Constantinople.

Phases:

  • 1547: Ivan IV, "the Terrible", crowned tsar. The conquest of Siberia began.
  • Peter the Great built a navy and a Western style state, founded Saint Petersburg in 1703 and took the title emperor in 1721.
  • Catherine the Great took Crimea and much of Poland-Lithuania.
  • Napoleon's invasion of 1812 failed, and Russia's army reached Paris.
  • The emancipation of the serfs in 1861.

War and defeat brought the Russian Revolution of 1917. Lenin's Bolsheviks took power, won a civil war and formed the Soviet Union in 1922. Under Stalin it was forced through collectivisation, fast industrial growth and mass terror, then lost tens of millions of people in defeating Nazi Germany. It became a nuclear superpower in the Cold War.

Gorbachev's reforms in the late 1980s ended in the break up of the Soviet Union in 1991. Russia carried on as its main successor; in 2022 it invaded Ukraine.
